title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
central_claims: miR-34a is underexpressed in CD44-positive prostate cancer cells, directly represses CD44, and inhibits stem-cell-associated tumor regeneration and metastasis.

source_manifest.title: Replication Study: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44.
source_manifest.finding: Direct prostate replication did not reproduce CD44/miR-34a expression or reporter results; in vivo transgene expression was lost, preventing a clean tumor-growth test.

source_manifest.title: Nanovesicle-mediated systemic delivery of microRNA-34a for CD44 overexpressing gastric cancer stem cell therapy.
source_manifest.finding: Nanovesicle miR-34a delivery suppressed CD44 and gastric cancer growth in mice, a different cancer setting.

source_manifest.title: Phase 1 study of MRX34, a liposomal miR-34a mimic, in patients with advanced solid tumours.
source_manifest.finding: MRX34 delivered miR-34a and modulated targets, but the phase 1 trial stopped early after severe immune toxicities and four deaths; this does not test the original prostate CD44 mechanism.

search_gaps: This is a bounded primary-evidence assessment, not an exhaustive adoption or clinical practice audit.
Failed or confounded selected experiments do not imply all claims in the original paper are false.
Exact first-publication version and separately linked supplements were not all verified.
MRX34 is a broader miR-34a product, so clinical toxicity was not converted into rejection of the original prostate CD44 claim or a blanket nonadoption label.
research.summary: Direct prostate replication did not reproduce CD44/miR-34a expression or reporter results; in vivo transgene expression was lost, preventing a clean tumor-growth test. Nanovesicle miR-34a delivery suppressed CD44 and gastric cancer growth in mice, a different cancer setting. MRX34 delivered miR-34a and modulated targets, but the phase 1 trial stopped early after severe immune toxicities and four deaths; this does not test the original prostate CD44 mechanism.
